extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and military personnel (Stars and Stripes/Honolulu edition)
extracted.subtask_description: Front‑page / homepage newspaper copy and briefs: a mix of dispatches, editorials, summaries and local military‑theater reporting aimed at informing and influencing a general and military readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldier-controlled editorial policy / editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper is edited, printed and distributed entirely by soldiers; the editorial policy is controlled by a board of five enlisted men who meet each day to discuss policy and decide on editorials, cartoons and stories on a basis of self-restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "We think we have the freest soldier newspaper in the world," said Managing Editor M/Sgt. Charles Avedon. Officers are assigned but act merely in an advisory capacity. Example staff names are given to illustrate enlisted control. The paper operated on self-restriction and has resisted suggestions of officer supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertive editorial stance toward authority (willingness to criticize brass)
rubrics_metrics.description: The newspaper takes an outspoken position against official double talk and brass interference, using its pages to rebuke Congress, criticize demobilization confusion, and uncover irregularities affecting soldiers and sailors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the paper 'lashed out against official double talk about demobilization' and 'has not hesitated to uncover any irregularities it finds.' It 'raps brass hats' and published stories that brought issues (e.g., the Stewart case) to public attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid resistance to attempted censorship or control
rubrics_metrics.description: When military officers attempted to impose publication controls (e.g., orders requiring that items be forwarded through the public relations office or suggestions of editorial supervision), the paper acted quickly to have such orders rescinded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific example: a colonel's notice requiring forwarding of news items through Public Relations was rescinded within 42 hours after Stars and Stripes intervened. Another attempted supervision suggestion was refused by higher command (Lt. Gen. Richardson refused suggested supervision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy and service orientation for enlisted audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper uses its influence among its circulation to advocate for and inform enlisted men, making clear that the paper 'is on their side with no reservations' and focusing coverage on issues affecting soldiers and sailors (pay, demobilization, grievances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper's editorial policy and topics (demobilization confusion, pay details, uncovering irregularities) are presented as serving enlisted readers' interests; circulation cited (~90,000 in the Pacific) demonstrates reach and influence.
